::: {.lead}
*Night Owl Games* has a new level for *Rooftop Rescue*: Pasha the cat jumps
from the roof, and the player must catch him with Nour's net. The producer
wants the storyboard of the level on Monday, with cutscene and gameplay
panels, timed, and checked. In lectures 9 to 11 you learned shots,
composition, flow, gameplay panels and the animatic. In this workshop you
put all of it together: you **play** the level first, then you storyboard it
from the brief to a checked version 2. Every section ends with a task, and
at the end you have your own board of a whole level.
:::

## Key terms

{{< glossary storyboard beat-sheet thumbnail-sketch panel-caption gameplay-storyboard hud player-input fail-state animatic storyboard-template >}}

## 12.1 Plan: the brief and the beat list

The producer's **brief** is short: what the level is, how long it may be,
and what must be in it. From the brief, the artist writes the **beat list**
before drawing anything (@fig-beats).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 12.1 — Brief and beat list"}
The **brief** says what the board is for: the moment, its length and what it
must show. The **beat list** is a numbered list of the beats (lecture 10),
each marked **cutscene** or **gameplay**, with the planned shot.
:::

The brief of *Cat Catch*: "Level 1, at most 30 seconds of cutscene and the
first try of play. Show the house in the flood and Pasha on the roof,
Salma's call, the rowing (swipe), the catch (tap), and both the success and
the fail."

![The beat list of level 1, Cat Catch: two cutscene beats, then gameplay with success and fail.](images/beat-list.png){#fig-beats width=96%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 12.1 — From the brief to beats"}
1. "The house in the flood and Pasha on the roof": a new place, a cutscene,
   a wide shot.
2. "Salma's call": a new speaker and a feeling, a close-up.
3. "The rowing (swipe)" and "the catch (tap)": two gameplay beats.
4. "Both the success and the fail": two panels, 5a and 5b.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Starting to draw before the beat list. Without the list, a board often
misses a beat that the brief asks for, for example the fail.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/cat-catch.html" poster="sims/cat-catch.png" title="Cat Catch: play level 1 before you board it" kind="game" height="620" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Play, then list"}
Play **Cat Catch** (above, or scan the QR code) once. Catch and miss at
least one cat.

1. Write the beat list of what you played: number, beat, cutscene or
   gameplay, shot.
2. Compare it with @fig-beats. What did you add or leave out?

*Your result:* your beat list with 6 to 8 beats.
:::

## 12.2 Draw: thumbnails, then clean panels

Drawing in two passes saves time: first quick **thumbnails** for every beat,
to check the shots; then clean panels with captions (@fig-steps).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 12.2 — Two passes"}
**Pass 1, thumbnails:** a small, fast sketch for every beat (one minute
each), to choose the shot and the composition. **Pass 2, clean panels:** the
chosen shots in 16:9 frames, with arrows, the HUD and input icons for
gameplay, and a full caption (shot, action or line, sound, time).
:::

![The workshop steps: brief, beat list, thumbnails, clean panels, animatic, review.](images/workshop-steps.png){#fig-steps width=96%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 12.2 — Panel 4, the catch"}
1. Thumbnail: the roof at the top right, the boat at the bottom, a dashed
   arrow for the fall.
2. Clean panel: a wide shot of the roof and the boat; the HUD (three hearts,
   the score); a tap icon near the net; an arrow for Pasha's fall.
3. Caption: "4 · Gameplay, wide. Pasha jumps; the player taps when he is in
   the ring. SFX: meow, whoosh. 3 s."
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Example 12.3 — A cutscene panel next to it"}
Panel 2 is a cutscene: a close-up of Salma. No HUD and no input icon: the
player only watches. Caption: "2 · Close-up. SALMA: Pasha, no! Stay there!
3 s."
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Putting the HUD on cutscene panels, or forgetting it on gameplay panels. The
HUD belongs only where the player plays.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/panel-composer.html" poster="sims/panel-composer.png" title="Panel Composer: build the gameplay panels of Cat Catch" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Draw the board"}
Use a storyboard template (paper) or PowerPoint, one panel per beat of your
list.

1. Draw the thumbnails, about one minute each.
2. Draw the clean panels with arrows, the HUD and input icons where the
   player plays, and full captions. First try the three tasks of **Panel
   Composer**.

*Your result:* a board of 6 to 8 clean panels with captions.
:::

## 12.3 Check: animatic, review and version 2

A first board is a draft. The artist plays it as an animatic, reads it with
the checklist, and makes a version 2 (@fig-review).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 12.3 — Review"}
A **review** plays the board as an animatic (is the time right?) and reads
it with the checklist: every beat drawn; shot sizes change with the
purpose; gameplay panels show the HUD and the input; success and fail
drawn; arrows and the same screen direction; the total time inside the
brief. Every "no" becomes a change in **version 2**.
:::

![The gameplay checklist of the review.](images/review-check.png){#fig-review width=96%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 12.4 — Sami's version 1"}
Sami's board has six panels: 4 s, 3 s, 6 s, 5 s, 4 s and 4 s.

1. Total: 26 s, inside the brief (30 s).
2. The checklist finds two "no": no fail panel, and no HUD on panel 3 (the
   rowing).
3. Version 2: Sami adds panel 5b (splash, one heart lost, 3 s) and the HUD on
   panel 3. New total: 29 s, still inside.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Fixing a board by adding text. If a panel does not show the idea, draw it
again; a caption cannot save an unclear picture.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Review your board"}
1. Make an animatic of your board in PowerPoint (lecture 11) and play it.
   Write the total time.
2. Read the board with the checklist of @fig-review. Change every "no", and
   write "version 2" on the board.

*Your result:* `cat-catch-board-v2.pptx` (or photos of the paper board) and
the list of your changes.
:::

## Case study: the Cat Catch board

The level *Cat Catch* is the mini-game you played in section 12.1: Pasha the
cat jumps from the roof of Salma's house, and the player taps when he is in
the ring above Nour's net; five cats, three hearts, +100 for each catch, a
splash and a lost heart for each miss. The brief asks for at most 30 seconds
of cutscene and first play, with both the success and the fail. The Game
challenge of the interactive lesson uses this level.

{{< sim file="sims/cat-catch.html" poster="sims/cat-catch.png" title="Cat Catch: play level 1 before you board it" kind="game" height="620" >}}

## Further reading

Schell, *The Art of Game Design*, 3rd ed., the chapters on prototypes and
iteration: a first version is made to be tested and changed.

## Exercises

1. What does a brief say? What does a beat list add?
2. Why write the beat list before drawing?
3. What are the two passes of drawing a board?
4. Which panels get a HUD and an input icon?
5. Write the caption of a gameplay panel in which the player taps to catch
   Pasha (3 s).
6. Write the caption of a cutscene panel with Salma's line "Pasha, no!"
   (2 s).
7. Name five points of the review checklist.
8. A board has 5, 4, 6, 3, 4 and 5 s. The brief allows 25 s. What do you do?
9. Why is a version 2 normal?
10. *Cat Catch*: which two panels must show the result of the catch?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. What the board is for, its length and what it must show; the beats, each with its kind and shot.
2. So that no beat of the brief is missing.
3. Thumbnails (fast sketches), then clean panels with captions.
4. Gameplay panels only.
5. "Gameplay, wide. Pasha jumps; the player taps when he is in the ring. SFX: meow. 3 s."
6. "Close-up. SALMA: Pasha, no! 2 s."
7. Every beat drawn; shot sizes change; HUD and input on gameplay; success and fail; arrows and screen direction; time inside the brief.
8. 27 s is too long: shorten or cut the longest panel with the least story (for example 6 s to 4 s).
9. A first board is a draft; the review always finds something to improve.
10. The success (+100) and the fail (splash, one heart lost).
:::
